Abstract.AbstractText: MicroRNAs have emerged as critical regulators in the pathogenesis of asthma. However, the role of microRNAs in asthma needs to be further elucidated. In this study, we found that miR-139-5p was greatly decreased in airway smooth muscle (ASM) cells from asthmatic humans as well as ASM cells stimulated with cytokines. Overexpression of miR-139-5p markedly suppressed ASM cell proliferation and promoted cell apoptosis, whereas knockdown of miR-139-5p had the opposite effect. Further study verified that Brg1, a chromatin remodeling factor, was upregulated in ASM cells treated with cytokines and acted as a direct target of miR-139-5p. Ectopic expression of Brg1 partially reversed the effect of miR-139-5p on cell proliferation and apoptosis. Moreover, overexpression of Brg1 restored miR-139-5p-induced downregulation of Akt and p70S6K phosphorylation. Together, these data indicate that miR-139-5p may function as a key regulator of ASM cell proliferation and apoptosis, potentially by targeting the Brg1 gene, and thus suggesting a potential role of miR-139-5p in the pathogenesis of asthma.
